newsitem.title: EGYPT: Millers lead Egyptian stock market upwards.
newsitem.headline: Millers lead Egyptian stock market upwards.

text.p: Milling shares led the Egyptian share market upwards again on Sunday but investors seemed more selective than in hectic bullish trading late last week.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index gained 3.74 points to close the day at 385.16 in trade worth an about average 48.665 million pounds ($14.34 million).
The partially privatised milling companies rose across the board in a confirmation that investors have overcome the jitters which hit the market during this month's steep correction.
"The mills are the barometer of the whole stock exchange. They always react very strongly to sentiment," said Mohamed Abdullah of brokers Intercapital.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills, among the most active shares of the day, added 2.46 pounds to close at 92.98. Central and West Delta Flour Mills gained 3.20 to 109.98.
The only exception was closely related company General Silos and Storage, which usually tracks the millers. It slipped 2.14 pounds to 107.00.

Abdullah said Medinet Nasr Housing and Development suffered from an announcement that shareholders will have to wait to qualify for their one-for-one free share. March 31 was the original cut-off date but the company has postponed this indefinitely because of a technical hitch.

The company will announce a new date as soon as the stock exchange has agreed to register the capital increase. Without this the new shares would have had to trade over-the-counter in parallel with the old ones. The shares lost 3.50 to 485.00.

Heliopolis Housing and Development announced a 25 percent increase in profits for the July-December period but the share fell sharply to 418.00 from 440.00. Abdullah said the nature of the real estate business made profit figures an unreliable guide to the value of such shares.

The broker said he noted strong demand for Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles, apparently on a newspaper report that the state would sell more shares and give up control of the partially privatised company. But trade in the stock was thin and the price did not change.
Banks and cements were mixed. Among the more active stocks, Commercial International Bank (CIB) rose 1.94 to 86.00 and Suez Cement gained 2.48 to 74.90.
The index for openly traded firms increased to 615.08 from 600.88 on Thursday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 261.21 from 260.88.
Out of the 73 shares traded on Sunday, 39 gained and 17 lost. Seventeen ended unchanged.
